summary: Sacks argues the chip stock correction is momentum-driven rather than fundamental, and that the AI CapEx boom is real with genuine ROI ahead, making the selloff temporary volatility amplified by leverage rather than a signal of deteriorating fundamentals.

summary: Friedberg argues 30-year Treasury yields crossing 5.2% — the highest in 20 years — driven by persistent inflation, $2T deficits, and fiscal deterioration make bonds unattractive relative to risk assets, though the high yield also makes equities harder to justify at current multiples.
quote: the 30-year Treasury yield, we just crossed 5.2% for the first time in 20 years. So you could buy US Treasuries that are paying you 5.2% a year for 30 years... I'm better off making 10% by owning federal government bonds.
